conventions.convention: The block representative λ is integral and dot-regular, with λ+ρ strictly dominant; standards are Δ(w·λ)=M(w·λ), and the antidominant label is w₀·λ.
Cartan generators have degree two. Classical invariant degrees dᵢ become page degrees 2dᵢ; the coinvariant top degree is 2∑(dᵢ−1).
Wall crossing acts on standard labels by right multiplication: θₛ sends the standard class w to w(1+s). For w=s₁⋯sₖ, the associated word functor is θₛₖ⋯θₛ₁.
V=Hom(P(w₀·λ),−) takes left End(P)ᵒᵖ-modules by precomposition; the commutative coinvariant identification makes these left C-modules.
The deformation ring R is S(h) localized at the origin. Relative weights are eigenmodules for h−τ(h), and the selected component is defined by its origin central-character block.
The central identification uses HCρ(z)(μ)=pr(z)(μ−ρ), followed by translation by λ+ρ. Its generic scalar on the x-standard branch is HCρ(z)(x(λ+ρ)+τ).

For type A, V(P(w·λ)) is the ungraded right reduction of B(w⁻¹). Polynomial shifts satisfy M(d)ⱼ=Mⱼ₊d; centered rank-one reduction has degrees −1 and 1. No grading of arbitrary category-O objects is asserted.
Standard-support ranks are measured on polynomial lifts before origin reduction; graph supports coalesce after reduction.
The batch assumes AC through its invariant-theory and category-O suppliers.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Over R=S(h) localized at the origin, each regular-block projective P(x·λ) has a unique projective lift P_R(x,λ), with the same deformed Verma-flag multiplicities; these are all indecomposables of the selected tensor component. Finite truncated projectives satisfy arbitrary-algebra-base-change Hom isomorphisms, and their Hom modules into finite Verma-filtered targets are finite free over R.

Assume AC. For the deformed antidominant projective, the shifted Harish-Chandra map a_λ: Z⊗R→R⊗_{R^W}R and the central action on End(P_R) are surjective with the same kernel, giving End(P_R)≅R⊗_{R^W}R. The right origin fiber is C; for dot stabilizer H the singular order is R^H⊗_{R^W}R, and translation out induces its inclusion into the regular order.

Assume AC. For every M in the regular integral block and every projective Q, the canonical map Hom_O(M,Q)→Hom_C(VM,VQ) is an isomorphism. V is fully faithful on projectives and faithful after passage to the quotient by its kernel Serre subcategory.
Assume AC. For every highest weight μ, the action induces U(g)/U(g)kerχ_μ≅End_C(M(μ))^{ad g-finite}; Ann M(μ)=U(g)kerχ_μ. For every finite-dimensional E, dim Hom_g(M(μ),E⊗M(μ))=dim E₀.

Assume AC. For a regular integral block and simple reflection s there is a natural isomorphism of left C-module functors Vθₛ≅C⊗_{C^s}V. In type A, Bₛ⊗_S C≅(C⊗_{C^s}C)(1); the right origin reduction of Bₛ has dimension two, whereas C⊗_{C^s}C has dimension 2|W|.

Assume AC. For dominant regular integral λ and a reduced word w=s₁⋯sₖ, θₛₖ⋯θₛ₁Δ(λ)≅P(w·λ)⊕⊕_{x<w}P(x·λ)^{m_x}, with m_x nonnegative integers. The top summand occurs once; every indecomposable projective occurs as a wall-word summand.

Assume AC. In a regular integral type-A block over C, V gives an equivalence from projectives to the additive category of ungraded summands of polynomial Bott-Samelson right reductions, with P(w·λ)↦B(w⁻¹)⊗_S C. The analogous ungraded equivalence holds for every complex semisimple regular integral block.

Assume AC. For a projective P in a regular integral type-A block and its prescribed polynomial lift B(P), (P:Δ(y·λ))=∑_d r_{y⁻¹,d}(B(P)). These are polynomial ranks before reduction, not an intrinsic separated-support filtration of V(P).

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says, without a middle-term qualification, 'Kernels, cokernels and extensions remain in this category'. Arbitrary U(g)⊗R-module extensions do not preserve the required relative-weight decomposition. For sl₂, induce the free rank-two Borel module with ev=ew=0, hv=(ξ+τ(h))v and hw=(ξ+τ(h))w+v. PBW gives an extension of Δ_R(ξ) by itself, but its highest space has a nonzero Jordan part for h−τ(h), so its middle term is not a relative-weight module. The opened published theorem thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed explicitly imposes the middle-term weight hypothesis and proves the corresponding ordinary counterexample in Step 5.1. The lifting proof must qualify its extension claim as occurring among relative-weight modules. This finding concerns that overstrong ancillary assertion; it does not itself refute the projective-lifting conclusion.

The singular part of the Statement and Proof 7.1 uses 'distinct cosets W/W_ν' without defining W_ν there. The inherited def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight uses W_ν for the integral-reflection group, which equals W for integral ν; the lifting argument instead requires Stab_W(ν+ρ). The later central-action lemma explicitly makes this distinction, but this supplier should fix its own stabilizer notation.

The final paragraph asserts: 'Every simple submodule of a Verma is itself a simple Verma: its universal Verma map into that Verma is injective.' This silently uses lem-a-nonzero-verma-homomorphism-is-injective, which is neither linked nor listed in this item's deps. Its opened two-step PBW/domain proof supplies the missing inference immediately. Declare that supplier or supply the elementary argument, since the resulting unique-socle assertion is used by the Struktursatz.
